what: The Lya version of the galaxy pair-count demo, on one patch of the fan at z = 2.1-3.0: QSO x QSO counted like galaxies (DD/RR); Lya x QSO and Lya x Lya as weighted averages of the flux fluctuation delta (no randoms), exactly as DESI's estimator (DESI 2024 IV Eq. 9-10).

units.positions: h^-1 Mpc, fan plane (fan.bin mapping: x = -r sin(RA - 182.5 deg), y = r cos(...), Dec projected out)
units.delta: delta_F = F / (mean F x continuum) - 1, projected (DESI 2024 IV Eq. 8)

cosmology.name: Planck 2018 base LCDM, DESI fiducial (flat; Omega_m includes one 0.06 eV neutrino)

patch.rule: annular sector of the fan slab from z = 2.1 (the fan's Lya-quasar threshold, flags bit 1) to z = 3.0; as wide at its middle radius as it is deep (a square in the fan plane, the galaxy patch's shape); centred on the fan's axis (RA 182.5 deg); the slab's full thickness (|Dec| < 1.25 deg). All zlya z > 2.1 quasars and all DR1 forest pixels (2.4 A) inside.
patch.why_this_size: the band holds most DR1 forest pixels and every quasar in it is a fan point; one patch this size gives a few billion pixel pairs (minutes to sum exactly) and detects the small-scale Lya signals, but not the BAO bump (the point of the scene)

bins.mu: mu = r_par / s, r_par = |r1 - r2| cos(theta / 2) (DESI 2024 IV Eq. 5); |mu|

estimator.qso_qso: xi = (DD / N_DD) / (RR / N_RR) - 1, N = n (n - 1) / 2 (the galaxy demo's normalisation)
estimator.lya_qso: xi = sum w_i w_Q delta_i / sum w_i w_Q over pixel-quasar pairs; each quasar's own forest excluded (DESI 2024 IV Eq. 10; picca xcf)
estimator.lya_lya: xi = sum w_i w_j delta_i delta_j / sum w_i w_j over pixel pairs on different sightlines (DESI 2024 IV Eq. 9; picca cf)
estimator.pixels: public DELTA_BLIND and WEIGHT at 0.8 A, rebinned x3 (picca Delta.rebin), weights x ((1+z)/(1+2.25))^(2.9-1), projected (picca Delta.project)
estimator.blinding: BLINDING = desi_y1 in every file read; in picca v9.0.0 this only names the column DELTA_BLIND, and picca_export treats desi_y1 as not blinded: the values are the measured deltas
estimator.errors: delete-one jackknife over 10 equal-angle strips across the patch (a sightline belongs to its quasar's strip); strips are about 71 h^-1 Mpc wide, narrower than the largest separations, so the errors at large s are approximate

qso_qso.random_rule: 20 x n_data, numpy PCG64 seed 20261015: RA uniform in the patch, sin(Dec) uniform in the slab, z drawn from the patch's quasars (with replacement); the first n_data are the ones drawn (randoms.x, .y); no angular completeness (quasars per strip: patch.quasars_per_jk_strip)

lya_qso.what_these_are: frac_delta_positive: share of the bin's pixel-quasar pairs whose pixel has delta > 0 (unweighted); mean_abs_delta: sum w w |delta| / sum w w. xi is the signed average; it is small because the deltas nearly cancel.

lya_lya.what_these_are: frac_product_positive: share of the bin's pixel pairs with delta_i delta_j > 0 (unweighted); mean_abs_product: sum w w |delta_i delta_j| / sum w w. xi is the signed average; it is small because the products nearly cancel.

galaxy_demo.geometry: 2D: separations in the fan plane (Dec projected out), as pairs.js counts them
galaxy_demo.source: survey/pairs.js preparePairs on the same fan.bin (node, at build time)

randoms.note: the first n_data randoms (drawn); RR uses all

sticks.rule: 8 per bin per type, the lowest seeded hash among pairs touching 48 seeded anchors (as the galaxy demo), preferring pairs drawn within 10% of their length on the fan (s_plane >= 0.9 s); pixels: weight >= the patch median (2.705); sorted by bin, then s
sticks.kind: computed (real pairs and their real values; the choice of which to draw is a seeded rule)

fields: fan_i (the quasar's fan.bin record; the sightline is its direction)
field.pixel_position: slot k: lambda = lam0 + k * step_A; z = lambda / 1215.67 - 1; r = chi(z) at the fan cosmology; fan-plane position = r * (x_i, y_i) / |(x_i, y_i)| with fan point i
field.delta_scale: delta = int8 / 50 (clipped to +-2.54); -128 = no pixel (masked or outside)
field.weight_scale: w = uint8 / 255 * 5.17644 (the patch's 99th percentile weight; clipped); 0 = no pixel
field.note: the projected delta that enters xi (rebinned 2.4 A pixels inside the patch); for drawing only

caveats: Separations are 3D (the slab is about 176 h^-1 Mpc thick here); the galaxy demo counts in 2D (Dec projected out), so its pair numbers are not like for like with these.
QSO x QSO randoms ignore DR1's angular completeness and the LSS weights; the forest needs no randoms.
Lya x QSO quasar weights follow DESI (gamma_Q = 1.44); DESI also models quasar redshift errors and the continuum-fitting distortion, which are part of the measured xi here as in DESI's data points.
The quasars are not spread evenly over the jackknife strips (patch.quasars_per_jk_strip); uniform randoms ignore that, which matters little at these errors.

checks.name: Lya x Lya: C kernel vs numpy brute force (3D Euclidean), seeded subset
Lya x QSO: C kernel + excluded own-forest pairs vs scipy cKDTree.count_neighbors (all pairs)
Lya x Lya: C kernel vs scipy cKDTree.count_neighbors (all pairs/2 minus same-sightline pairs)
QSO x QSO: DD from the C kernel vs scipy cKDTree.count_neighbors

method_sources.paper: DESI 2024 IV (arXiv:2404.03001v3) Sec. 3.1-3.3: Eq. 5 (r_par, r_perp), 6 (weights, gamma_Lya 2.9), 7-8 (projection), 9 (auto, different spectra only), 10-11 (cross, gamma_Q 1.44); Fig. 11 list (rebin 3 pixels in the main analysis)

files.used: read_deltas: rebin, then weights *= ((1+z)/(1+z_ref))**(alpha-1), then project; quasar weights
neighbours exclude the same LOS (delta.thingid != other_delta.thingid)
neighbours exclude the forest's own quasar (obj.thingid != delta.thingid)
get_data: the delta column is named DELTA_BLIND when Forest.blinding != 'none'; values unchanged

cite: DESI Collaboration et al. 2026, AJ 171, 285 (arXiv:2503.14745) - DR1
DESI 2024 IV (arXiv:2404.03001) - DR1 Lya BAO: zlya, deltas, estimators
Ramirez-Perez et al. 2024 (the Lya deltas VAC reference on its page)
